Vertiv VRT is scheduled to report third-quarter 2026 results on Oct. 28, with the Americas segment expected to remain the company's primary growth engine. Robust investments in artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure, accelerating hyperscale data center deployments and sustained demand for advanced power and thermal management solutions are likely to support another strong quarter for the region.

The Americas remains Vertiv's largest revenue-generating region and a key growth driver. In the second quarter of 2026, regional revenue increased 29% year over year to $2.07 billion, with organic sales up 21%. Adjusted operating profit reached $571 million, while adjusted operating margin expanded 360 basis points, reflecting favorable commercial execution and operational efficiencies.

The company provided guidance reflecting continued confidence in the Americas' ability to drive results. For the third quarter of 2026, Vertiv expects organic sales growth in the Americas in the high-30% range, representing a significant acceleration from the preceding quarter. The company is expanding manufacturing capabilities through five major plant expansions across the Americas. Additional capacity coming online should speed backlog conversion and support delivery of increasingly complex infrastructure projects. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for Americas revenues is pegged at $2.52 billion, representing a 21.6% sequential increase.

VRT Benefits From Manufacturing and Cooling Portfolio

Vertiv's expanding portfolio and acquisitions are expected to drive growth in the quarter to be reported. Strategic acquisitions, such as PurgeRite, have strengthened Vertiv's liquid cooling and system-level service offerings, which are critical for modern data centers.

Vertiv's expanding portfolio of integrated power and thermal management solutions, including SmartRun and OneCore, is another positive. Growing adoption of high-density AI computing infrastructure is increasing demand for scalable power distribution, liquid cooling and prefabricated data center solutions. These offerings strengthen Vertiv's competitive positioning against Super Micro Computer SMCI and Amphenol APH and create opportunities for larger customer engagements.

Acquisitions are also expected to benefit VRT's portfolio. Vertiv recently completed its acquisition of King Environmental Services Ltd. ("KES"), a Europe-based provider of fluid management, commissioning and load-testing services for high-density, liquid-cooled data centers.

The acquisition strengthens Vertiv's thermal management capabilities across Europe, the Middle East and Africa, complementing its North American presence established through the PurgeRite acquisition in 2025. KES brings expertise in fluid treatment, system validation and thermal load testing, helping customers improve cooling efficiency, operational reliability and infrastructure readiness. The acquisition supports Vertiv's strategy to address growing cooling requirements in AI-driven data centers.

title: Can SMCI's DCBBS and DLC Improve its Financial Outlook in 2026?

Can SMCI's DCBBS and DLC Improve its Financial Outlook in 2026?

Trading disclosure

Super Micro Computer SMCI is moving beyond stand-alone servers toward complete Data Center Building Block Solutions (DCBBS). DCBBS integrates Graphics Processing Units (GPU) and Central Processing Units (CPU) servers, enterprise storage, direct liquid cooling, power infrastructure, high-speed switches, networking, data-center management software and lifecycle services.

The combination of modular engineering and broad silicon support helps Super Micro Computer respond to shorter hardware cycles. It also supports the company's strategy of offering application-optimized systems across enterprise, cloud, AI and edge workloads. Management said the model is intended to reduce customer time-to-deployment and time-to-online by providing a more integrated data-center build.

SMCI is also expanding software tools such as SuperCloud Composer, Super Micro Data Center Manager and Super Micro Orchestration Manager, while adding proactive service capabilities. Broader software and service attachment can deepen the customer relationship and increase the amount of infrastructure supplied per project. SMCI expects more software features and service products to come online early in fiscal 2027, extending the DCBBS strategy beyond hardware integration.

Furthermore, rising rack density is increasing the importance of advanced cooling in AI data centers, and Super Micro Computer continues to expand direct liquid-cooling (DLC) capabilities. SMCI is producing liquid-cooled rack-scale systems for current AI platforms with its DLC production lines supporting 250kW-class racks. SMCI's fiscal 2027 capacity plan calls for more than 6,000 racks per month, including more than 3,000 DLC racks.

Liquid cooling is integrated into the broader DCBBS portfolio alongside chilled doors, cooling distribution units and other infrastructure. This capability gives Super Micro Computer a broader role in high-density deployments as customers move from server purchases toward complete rack-scale systems.

How Competitors Fare Against SMCI

SMCI is at a crossroads with major players like Hewlett Packard Enterprise HPE and Dell Technologies DELL. Hewlett Packard Enterprise is providing enterprises with an integrated AI infrastructure portfolio spanning hardware, software and cloud management to scale generative AI, agentic AI and high-performance computing workloads.

HPE combines compute, storage, networking and GreenLake platform with NVIDIA's GPUs, CPUs, networking technologies and AI Enterprise software. The integrated offering allows enterprises to build and manage AI environments through a unified platform. Dell Technologies, meanwhile, is pursuing a broader ecosystem strategy through its Dell AI Factory.

Super Micro Computer (SMCI) is expected to deliver a year-over-year increase in earnings on higher revenues when it reports results for the quarter ended September 2026. This widely-known consensus outlook gives a good sense of the company's earnings picture, but how the actual results compare to these estimates is a powerful factor that could impact its near-term stock price.

The stock might move higher if these key numbers top expectations in the upcoming earnings report, which is expected to be released on November 3. On the other hand, if they miss, the stock may move lower.

While management's discussion of business conditions on the earnings call will mostly determine the sustainability of the immediate price change and future earnings expectations, it's worth having a handicapping insight into the odds of a positive EPS surprise.

Zacks Consensus Estimate

This server technology company is expected to post quarterly earnings of $1.24 per share in its upcoming report, which represents a year-over-year change of +254.3%.

Revenues are expected to be $15.77 billion, up 214.3% from the year-ago quarter.

Estimate Revisions Trend

The consensus EPS estimate for the quarter has been revised 6.35% higher over the last 30 days to the current level. This is essentially a reflection of how the covering analysts have collectively reassessed their initial estimates over this period.

Investors should keep in mind that an aggregate change may not always reflect the direction of estimate revisions by each of the covering analysts.

Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise Chart for SMCI
Earnings Whisper

Estimate revisions ahead of a company's earnings release offer clues to the business conditions for the period whose results are coming out. This insight is at the core of our proprietary surprise prediction model -- the Zacks Earnings ESP (Expected Surprise Prediction).

The Zacks Earnings ESP compares the Most Accurate Estimate to the Zacks Consensus Estimate for the quarter; the Most Accurate Estimate is a more recent version of the Zacks Consensus EPS estimate. The idea here is that analysts revising their estimates right before an earnings release have the latest information, which could potentially be more accurate than what they and others contributing to the consensus had predicted earlier.

Thus, a positive or negative Earnings ESP reading theoretically indicates the likely deviation of the actual earnings from the consensus estimate. However, the model's predictive power is significant for positive ESP readings only.

Dell Stock Sinks 21% in a Week After Barclays Downgrade: Is the AI Rally Losing Steam? ©Lisa Fotios from Pexels and ispyfriend from Getty Images Signature via Canva
Key Takeaways

Dell stock fell 21% over the five trading sessions ending October 19, significantly underperforming the Nasdaq 100.

Barclays downgraded Dell, questioning whether higher memory prices rather than stronger enterprise AI demand are driving revenue growth.

Dell reported $47 billion in quarterly revenue and a $95 billion AI backlog, although free cash flow declined 47%.

Dell traded near 16x forward earnings, making cash flow performance a key test of its valuation.

Dell Technologies (DELL:NYSE) shares fell 21% over the five trading sessions ending October 19, compared with a 3.7% decline in the Nasdaq 100.

The biggest drop came October 14, when Dell plunged 11.3% following a Barclays downgrade. AI server competitor Super Micro Computer (SMCI:NASDAQ) fell 19.7% over the same period, highlighting broader weakness across AI infrastructure stocks.

Higher interest rate expectations and concerns about AI hardware valuations added pressure. Despite the correction, Dell remained up approximately 262% in 2026 through October 19.

Why Barclays Is Questioning Dell's AI Growth

Barclays analyst Tim Long downgraded Dell from Overweight to Equal Weight and lowered his price target from $603 to $574, citing valuation concerns and limited evidence of a meaningful AI spending inflection among enterprise customers.

The bank questioned how much of Dell's revenue growth comes from higher memory prices rather than stronger underlying demand.

If memory prices stabilize, revenue growth could slow even while AI server demand remains healthy.

Dell's fiscal second-quarter revenue increased 58% to $47 billion, while AI orders reached a record $60.9 billion and its backlog climbed to $95 billion.

Wall Street expects revenue of approximately $193 billion for the fiscal year ending January 2027 and $229 billion the following year.

Dell Technologies (DELL): revenue, actual and consensus estimates, $ billions, fiscal 2024–2029 (years to January) (TIKR)
Dell's Next Major Test Is Cash Flow

Dell generated $986 million in free cash flow during its fiscal second quarter, down 47% year over year, as customer financing receivables absorbed $6.67 billion in cash.

Analysts expect approximately $12 billion in full-year free cash flow. With $4.10 billion generated in the first half, Dell would need roughly $7.9 billion in the second half to meet that estimate.

That makes cash conversion an important test as Dell works through its growing AI backlog.

Is Dell Stock Attractively Valued After the Selloff?

Dell's forward P/E declined from an August peak above 26x to around 16x as of October 16, but remained above its five-year average of approximately 12x.

title: Super Micro Computer Just Gave Its Investors Fantastic News

Super Micro Computer (NASDAQ:SMCI) has earnings coming up and is scheduled to release its first-quarter numbers for fiscal 2027 on Nov. 3. And last week, the company gave its investors some great news: its results are going to be better than expected, with both revenue and gross margins coming in considerably higher than what they previously forecasted.

The company, which has been an integral player in the data center build-out, selling crucial artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure, including servers and storage solutions, has benefited from significant demand for its products in recent years. This year, it's up around 12%, and a strong quarter could potentially light a fire under this lowly valued tech stock.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Image source: Getty Images.

Revenue to be nearly four times what it was a year ago

Super Micro's upcoming quarterly results will be for the period ending Sept. 30. The company projects revenue in the range of $18.5 billion to $19.5 billion, a significant increase from its earlier guidance of $14.5 billion to $15.5 billion. Not only is that a big upgrade to the top line, but the tech company also expects its gross margins to be in the range of 12% to 12.5% -- higher than its previous projection of 10.4% to 10.8%.

These are extremely promising developments for investors for a couple of reasons. The first is the sheer growth. At $19 billion, the mid-point of its revenue forecast would mean that its top line will be nearly quadruple the $5 billion it generated a year ago. Margins have also been a key concern for investors, and if they are improving yet again, it's another encouraging sign that the business is making progress in the right direction.

Is Super Micro stock a steal of a deal?

Although Super Micro is experiencing significant growth, the stock itself isn't that expensive. Based on analyst projections, it's trading at a forward price-to-earnings multiple of just eight. The company has had accounting issues and governance concerns hanging over it in recent years, which may partially explain why the stock isn't trading at a higher valuation. Plus, there are concerns that a tech bubble has formed, and if demand for servers and other AI infrastructure slows, there could be significant headwinds for the stock.
